correctness.rationale: The rooted vertex/block incidence forest gives a true partition of neighbor contributions. For an omitted parent, the clique has zero or one selected child; for a selected parent, its clique children are either all omitted (each with zero descendant-selected neighbors) or all included. Each vertex combines zero- or one-selected-neighbor contributions over disjoint blocks. Leaf initialization and root sum prove exactness by induction; 937 constructed and 8,367 all-labelled finite block graphs through order six were compared coefficientwise with brute force.

originality.rationale: The 2026 primary manuscript computes scalar P3-convex-set counts on trees and threshold graphs and uses general exponential algorithms, whereas this result obtains the full cardinality polynomial on all block graphs via a constant-state clique-incidence-tree circuit. The other block-graph sources study distinct invariants/convexities. Real semantically targeted searches found no implication covering this theorem; a missed equivalent recurrence remains a risk.
residual_risks: The older Carathéodory paper and the digitally convex thesis were only accessible in abstract form; they cannot support whole-document noncoverage assertions.
Unindexed papers on two-neighbor bootstrap percolation fixed points or clique-tree constraint enumeration could contain equivalent recurrences.
Arithmetic circuits are distinct from expanded-coefficient bit-complexity bounds; the theorem claims only the former.

value.rationale: The 2026 counting problem is #P-complete on split graphs, yet the newly identified entire block-graph class (including unbounded-size clique blocks and unbounded treewidth) has an explicit linear-size polynomial arithmetic circuit and exact size distribution. The divide-free constant-boundary-state method and all-parameter clique-bouquet formula reveal enumerative structure absent from the known tree-only scalar recurrence. This is a natural, motivated tractable classification rather than arbitrary isolated parameter values.
